{{nihongo|'''Kunitsuhiko-no-Mikoto Shrine'''|國津比古命神社}} is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} in Hattachi, {{ill|Matsuyama|Q200022|qid=Q200022}} (former {{ill|Hōjō, Ehime|Q94789|qid=Q94789}}), {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|Q123376|qid=Q123376}}. Its former rank was {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}. It stands atop a {{ill|Kofun|Q1141225|qid=Q1141225}} (Kunitsuhiko-no-Mikoto Shrine Kofun; total length 50 m). {{nihongo|'''Kunitsuhiko-no-Mikoto Shrine'''|國津比古命神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iyo Province]].

== Overview ==
The enshrined deity is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}}. He is also called Amaterukuniteruhikoame-no-hoakari-kushitama-nigihayahi-no-Mikoto. Although it is called Kunitsuhiko-no-Mikoto Shrine, the deity is an {{ill|Amatsukami and Kunitsukami|ja|天津神・国津神|ko|아마쓰카미·구니쓰카미|zh|天津神與國津神|qid=Q11442793|lt=Amatsukami}}.

{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Umashimaji-no-Mikoto}}, Mononobe no Asari no Mikoto, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto|qid=Q317997}} are also enshrined.

It faces {{ill|Kushitamahime Shrine|Q134888243|qid=Q134888243}}. Locally, the two shrines together are called "Kazahaya-no-Miya Ōujigami."

== Annual festival ==
On the first day of the October three-day holiday, the Godōza Festival is held; on the second day, the Shinkō Festival is held.

Called the Kazahaya Fire Festival, it includes throwing a mikoshi down stone steps, and is one of Japan's three major "rough mikoshi" festivals<ref>The other two are Miyagi's "Hote Matsuri" and Himeji's "Nada no Kenka Matsuri".</ref>.
